A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that it is possible to train a text-to-SQL parser with a non-deterministic oracle and that this can lead to a significant improvement in the performance of a model.

we present a sequence-toaction parsing approach for the text-to-SQL task that can effectively handle the multiple target SQL queries with the similar semantics, and we also present an oracle design that can better guide the learning of the models.
we propose an incremental sequence-to-action parsing model for the natural language-to-SQL task that is trained with non-determinism and can be further boosted by execution-guided decoding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is beneficial to train sequence-to-action parsers with non-determinism in mind, even if the final model is deterministic.
by using non-deterministic training, we can train more robust and accurate text-to-SQL models that are less sensitive to the choice of the target query.

by using non-deterministic training, the models are better able to capture the inherent ambiguity of the task and learn to generalize to new unseen examples with different but semantically equivalent SQL queries.
